column1: It is often argued that [young sports competitions should be banned because many young people fear losing]. In my opinion, I completely [disagree] with this statement. This is because [competitive sports teach children how to handle failure] and [help them develop essential physical and teamwork skills].
column3: Many young people do not enjoy competitive sports because they are afraid of losing. For that reason, youth sports competitions should be banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

column1: First of all, the main reason for my view is that [facing failure is a necessary life lesson for youngsters]. This means that [losing a sports match teaches children that defeat is normal and encourages them to practice harder next time]. As a result, [young people build strong emotional resilience and learn how to manage disappointment in everyday situations]. For example, [when a soccer team loses a game, players learn to support each other instead of giving up]. Therefore, [participating in competitive sports helps prepare children for difficulties in adulthood].

Furthermore, another important point to consider is that [competitions bring great physical and social benefits]. In other words, [preparing for matches motivates teenagers to exercise regularly, stay away from video games and lead active lifestyles]. This leads to [better physical health, strong teamwork, and effective communication skills among peers]. For instance, [school tournaments are the best place to discover and nurture talented young athletes for national teams]. Consequently, [banning youth tournaments would eliminate great opportunities for talent development and health exercise].

In conclusion, [banning sports competitions for young people] brings significant [negative] impacts. The primary reasons are [healthy competition teaches valuable coping skills] and [promotes physical fitness among youth]. Therefore, I reaffirm my view that I strongly [disagree] with this idea.

It is often argued that [Globalization brings great benefits to economies, but its drawbacks should not be overlooked]. In my opinion, I agree with this statement only to some extent. While [global trade creates valuable economic growth for many nations], I also believe that [it causes serious problems for domestic businesses and workers].
column3: Globalization is positive for economies but its negative sides should not be ignored. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

column1: On the one hand, I agree that [globalization provides strong economic opportunities]. The main reason is that [opening international markets allows companies to sell products worldwide and attract foreign investments]. As a result, [many countries can build modern infrastructure, expand production, and create millions of jobs]. For example,  [developing nations like Vietnam have received huge foreign capital to build electronics factories and hire local workers]. Therefore, this shows that [globalization brings enormous financial benefits and improves national living standards].

On the other hand, I disagree with the idea that [globalization only brings positive outcomes without serious drawbacks]. This is because [multinational corporations often dominate local markets with cheaper mass-produced goods]. Consequently, [small local businesses cannot compete and are forced to shut down]. For instance, [cheap imported clothes and food often put local manufacturers and traditional farmers out of businesses]. Therefore, [ignoring these negative impacts can cause rising unemployment and widen the gap between the rich and the poor].

In conclusion, while [globalization promotes international trade and creates economic development], it is not entirely true because [it harms vulnerable local companies and workers]. Therefore, I hold the view that this idea should only be accepted to a certain extent.

It is often argued that [the intended purpose of a building is far more important than its external look]. In my opinion, I agree with this statement only to some extent. While [practical usability is necessary for daily living], I also believe that [outward appearance plays a vital role in local tourism and cultural identity].
column3: When designing a building, the most important factor is the intended use of the building rather than its outward appearance. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

column1: On the one hand, I agree that [function must be a top priority during construction]. The main reason is that [buildings need to provide a comfortable, safe, and productive environment for occupants]. As a result, [schools, offices, and factories must have adequate ventilation, quiet study space and stable structures]. Therefore, this shows that [meeting the intended function is fundamental for any construction project].

On the other hand, I disagree with the idea that [external appearance is insignificant]. This is because [iconic and creative architecture enhances urban beauty and attracts millions of international travelers]. Consequently, [well-designed public buildings help boost local businesses and create recognizable symbols for an entire city]. For instance, [the Sydney Opera House and Eiffel Tower are world-famous tourist attractions primarily because of their striking outer appearance]. Therefore, [visual design holds great economic and cultural value that architects should not overlook].

In conclusion, while [practical function ensures user safety and daily convenience], it is not entirely true because [it creates cultural pride and tourist revenue]. Therefore, I hold the view that this idea should only be accepted to a certain extent.

While [top athletes earn far more than vital workers like doctors or teachers], I also believe that [their high salaries reflect the massive commercial profits they generate and their short career spans].
column3: Do you agree or disagree that professional athletes are overpaid?

column1: On the one hand, I agree that [salaries in the professional sports industry are extremely inflated]. The main reason is that [playing sports is an entertainment activity rather than an essential public service]. As a result, [it creates a sense of injustice when sports stars earn millions of dollars while healthcare staff and police officers receive modest wages].For example, [a premier football player can make more money in one week than a devoted surgeon earns in ten years] .Therefore, this shows that [the compensation for athletes is disproportionate to their actual contribution to society].

On the other hand, I disagree with the idea that [these salaries are completely unjustified]. This is because [the global sports industry generates enormous revenues from broadcasting rights, ticket sales, and commercial sponsorships]. Consequently, [talented athletes simply receive their fair share of the massive profits that their performances create]. For instance, [professional players must undergo rigorous training from a very young age and face the constant risk of career-ending physical injuries before age thirty-five]. Therefore, [high earnings represent a fair reward for rare talent and very short working career].

In conclusion, while [the enormous pay gap between sports stars and essential workers seems unfair], it is not entirely true because [athletes operate within a highly profitable global entertainment industry]. Therefore, I hold the view that this policy/idea should only be accepted to a certain extent.

It is often argued that [sports competitions for youngsters should be eliminated because fear of defeat discourages many participants]. In my opinion, I agree with this statement only to some extent. While [excessive pressure to win can cause stress for sensitive children], I also believe that [completely banning sports events is unnecessary and harmful].
column3: Many young people do not enjoy competitive sports because they are afraid of losing. For that reason, youth sports competitions should be banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

column1: On the one hand, I agree that [intense competition can negatively affect children’s psychology]. The main reason is that [overly ambitious coaches and parents often put extreme pressure on young athletes to win every game]. As a result, [children who fail to win medals feel embarrassed, lose self-confidence, and eventually quit playing sports altogether]. For example, [many children cry and experience severe anxiety before school matches due to high parental expectations]. Therefore, this shows that [an excessive focus on winning can ruin the fun and enjoyment of physical activities].

On the other hand, I disagree with this idea that [banning competitions is the right solution]. This is because [competitive games motivate young players to set personal goals, train consistently, and respect game rules]. Consequently, [children earn valuable life lessons like discipline, perseverance, and fair play that classroom books cannot teach]. For instance, [participating in local running or swimming contests helps young runners build strong willpower and pride in their personal progress]. Therefore, [schools should reform the way competitions are organized instead of banning  them completely].

In conclusion, while [the fear of losing and high pressure can discourage some young participants], it is not entirely true because [competitions should be banned because they teach essential life skills]. Therefore, I hold the view that this idea should only be accepted to a certain extent.

It is often argued that [acquiring a foreign language remains beneficial even with numerous modern translation programs available]. In my opinion, I agree with this statement only to some extent. While [digital translation devices are fast and practical for simple daily tasks], I also believe that [mastering a language is indispensable for deeper communication and career success].
column3: Although there is a lot of translation software available, learning a language could still be advantageous. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

column1: On the one hand, I agree that [modern translation tools can help people manage basic situations without studying for years]. The main reason is that [artificial intelligence and translation software can instantly convert voice, text and photos into local languages at low cost]. As a result, [tourists and casual users can read road signs, order restaurant meals, and ask for directions effortlessly]. For example, [a traveler visiting Tokyo can easily navigate train stations just by using a phone camera to translate signs]. Therefore, this shows that [basic communications needs can be solved quickly by software without formal language learning].

On the other hand, I disagree with the idea that [digital apps make learning a new language completely unnessary]. This is because [mobile applications cannot replace emotional subtleties, local humor, and professional discussions]. Consequently, [using a digital phone for every sentence creates awkward pauses and shows a lack of commitment in formal environments]. For instance, [international diplomats and business leaders must speak fluently to build long-term relationships rather than relying on automated gadgets]. Therefore, [direct language study is still essential for authentic human understanding and career development].

In conclusion, while [translation tools provide great convenience for tourists in basic daily tasks], it is not entirely true because [they can replace the true value of language learning]. Therefore, I hold the view that this policy/idea should only be accepted to a certain extent.

In recent years, there has been a noticeable shift towards [urban residents living by themselves or in small nuclear families instead of extended households]. Although I understand why some people view this as a negative development, I still consider it to be a largely positive trend.
column3: In many countries today, people in cities either live alone or in small family units, rather than in large, extended family groups. Is this a positive or negative trend?

column1: There are several reasons why this trend can be seen as a negative development. The primary concern is that [individuals living alone or in small units often experience loneliness and isolation]. For instance, [elderly people who live away from their children and grandchildren may lack daily care and emotional support]. In addition, [small households miss out on shared family responsibilities like childcare]. This means that [working parents must pay high fees for babysitters or daycares without help from grandparents]. As a result, [living independently creates both emotional stress and heavy financial burdenrs].

Nevertheless, I am in favour of the opinion that this is a positive development for several reasons. Firstly, [living independently gives individuals greater personal freedom and privacy].  For example, [young professionals can organize their schedules, hobbies, and living spaces without family conflicts]. Secondly, [smaller household sizes reduce daily arguments over money and lifestyle differences]. Consequently, [family members maintain more peaceful and respectful relationships with one another] .Therefore, [this trend fosters personal development and modern living comfort].

In conclusion, despite understanding why some critics view [independent city living] as a negative trend due to [loneliness and lack of daily support].  I still believe that its positive contributions to [personal autonomy and reduced domestic conflict] are far more profound. Therefore, I hold the belief that this is ultimately a positive development for modern society.

In recent years, there has been a noticeable shift towards [younger leaders in many organizations]. This phenomenon is primarily driven by several key factors. In my opinion, I strongly believe that [this is a positive development for society].
column3: Leaders of all kinds are often younger now than in the past. What are the reasons for this? Is it a positive or a negative development?

column1: First of all, there are clear reasons why [having younger leaders is becoming more common today]. The primary reason is that [[young individuals can easily acquire modern knowledge through the advancement of technology and artificial intelligence]. This means that [they quickly learn digital tools and technical skills that modern corporations urgently require]. In addition, [young professionals are eager to demonstrate their personal capabilities and work with great dedication]. For example, [they are willing to work overtime and travel frequently because they usually have fewer family responsibilities]. Therefore, [these factors together encourage companies to appoint younger individuals to leadership roles].

On the other hand, I consider this trend to be a welcome and positive development. The primary benefit is that [young leaders bring abundant energy, creativity, and enthusiasm to organizations]. In other words, [they are open to new business concepts and adapt quickly to fast-changing market environments]. Furthermore, [hiring younger executives allows companies to reduce labour costs compared to retaining senior staff with high salary expectations]. For instance, [start-ups and tech firms can reinvest these savings into research and product innovation]. Thus, this offers valuable opportunities for [economic growth and modernization].

In conclusion, [the rise of young leaders is mainly caused by quick access to modern technology and strong personal ambition]. Moreover, it brings clear advantages such as [high energy, innovation, and cost efficiency for enterprises]. Therefore, I hold the belief that this trend is ultimately a positive development for modern society.

It is often argued that [all undergraduate degrees should include a period of studying in another nation or doing an internship]. Although this trend brings some clear [drawbacks], I strongly believe that its [advantages] are much more significant.
column3:
All university undergraduate courses should include a period of time spent studying abroad or doing a work placement.
Do you think the advantages of this would outweigh the disadvantages?

column1: On the one hand, there are several [disadvantages] associated with this development. The [main problem] is that [travelling abroad or relocating for work creates heavy financial stress]. This means that [students must pay expensive living costs such as apartment rent, transport, and daily meals]. In addition, [finding an internship position can be very competitive and difficult for some students]. For example, [individuals who cannot secure a company placement quickly may delay their graduation time]. Therefore, this can [cause difficulties and anxiety for] [poorer students].

On the other hand, I believe that the [benefits] are far more [important]. Firstly, [hands-on work experience helps undergraduates understand their future professions better than classroom lectures alone]. Consequently, [job applicants with practical training stand out and easily get hired by big companies]. Secondly, [living in a new environment helps young people build independence, adaptability and fluent communication skills]. For instance, [interacting with international friends teaches valuable teamwork skills that modern employers actively seek]. Thus, this [offers valuable opportunities for] [personal growth and long-term career success].

In conclusion, while [compulsory international study or internships] can [create some problems] regarding [living costs and time pressure], its [positive] impacts on [employability and personal development] are much greater. Therefore, I reaffirm my view that the [advantages] clearly outweigh the [disadvantages].

It is argued that [encouraging people to live a healthy lifestyle is the best way to reduce healthcare costs]. In my opinion, I completely agree with this statement. This is because [a healthy lifestyle can prevent physical diseases] and [improves mental health].
column3: Health professionals argue that promoting a healthy lifestyle is the key to reducing healthcare costs. Do you agree and disagree?

column1: First of all, the main reason for my view is that [regular exercise and a balanced diet protect people from severe illnesses] This means that, [if people eat well and exercise regularly, they are less likely to develop problems such as obesity, heart disease and diabetes]. These health problems are very common and very expensive to treat over a long time. For example, [maintaining a daily workout routine keeps blood pressure stable]. As a result, [people do not need to see a doctor often or take a lot of medication]. Therefore, this shows that [good physical habits help to reduce costs of their treatment].

Furthermore, another important point to consider is that [a healthy life not only prevents chronic physical diseases but also strongly enhances mental health]. In other words, [ encouraging habits like regular physical activity and enough  sleep, everyone can reduce mental stress and depression effectively]. These mental health problems are common problems that lead to an increase in the number of hospital admissions. For instance, [employees who practice yoga or jog after work rarely experience mental burnout]. Thus, [this can bring positive results for the healthcare system by saving national medical budgets].

In conclusion, [encouraging a healthy lifestyle] brings significant impacts. The primary reasons are [eating well, exercising, and taking care of mental health can prevent diseases] and [reduce overall treatment expenses]. Therefore, I reaffirm my view that I strongly agree with this idea.

It is often argued that [once children begin school, teachers have the greatest impact on their intellectual and social development]. In my opinion, I agree with this statement only to some extent. While [teachers contribute largely to the growth of students], I also believe that [family habits and the peer environment] are equally vital.
column3: Once children start school, teachers have more influence on their intellectual and social development. To what extent do you agree and disagree?

column1: On the one hand, I agree that [teachers play a significant role in developing children’s minds and behaviors]. The main reason is that [besides academic subjects, teachers also share moral lessons and life experiences to guide students away from bad actions]. As a result, [students build good discipline, distinguish right from wrong, and achieve personal growth]. In addition, [schools provide useful career guidance and practical skills]. This means that [students can prepare well for stable jobs in the future to support themselves and their families]. Therefore, this shows that [teachers strongly shape student’s knowledge and social capabilities].

On the other hand, I disagree with the idea that [teachers have more influence than all other factors]. This is because [the daily habits and attitudes of parents still heavily direct children’s behaviors at home]. For instance, [if parents often smoke cigarettes or use vulgar language, their children are very likely to copy these negative behaviors]. Moreover, [peer pressure and friends at school directly shape a child’s character. If youngsters study in a classroom where all peers strive for high scores, they will be strongly motivated to study hard]. Therefore, [parental upbringing and friend circles play an equally decisive role in children’s development].

In conclusion, while [teachers greatly foster children’s academic abilities and ethical awareness], it is not entirely true that [they are the sole influence because family examples and peer environments are just as important]. Therefore, I hold the view that this statement should only be accepted to a certain extent.

It is often argued that [schools are no longer necessary in modern times because children can learn everything at home via the internet]. In my opinion, I completely disagree with this statement. This is because [young students need a structured school curriculum to guide their learning] and [schools provide an essential environment for making friends and developing social skills].
column3: In the modern world, schools are no longer necessary because there is so much information available through the internet that children can study just as well at home. To what extent do you agree and disagree?

column1: First of all, the main reason for my view is that [educational institutions provide a standard curriculum designed for each age group]. This means that [educational experts have organized lessons systematically so that children can absorb knowledge step by step]. As a result, [young children do not get confused or overwhelmed by the massive amount of unverified information online]. For example, [primary school students lack the ability to filter materials on the internet and will easily feel stressed if they must study alone]. Therefore, [structured school programs protect young learners from study pressure and ensure effective education].

Furthermore, another important point to consider is that [schools are irreplaceable places for social interaction and peer connection]. In other words, [attending school gives children daily opportunities to make friends, communicate with classmates of their age, and share common interests]. This leads to [essential social skills like teamwork, empathy and emotional growth]. For instance, [playing sports like football or badminton with classmates after school helps students build strong friendships and improve physical health at the same time]. Consequently, [home studying cannot replace schools because it causes social isolation and deprives children of real friendships].

In conclusion, [replacing schools with home internet learning] brings significant negative consequences. The primary reasons are [youngsters need age-appropriate curriculums to learn without stress] and [schools offer vital peer interaction]. Therefore, I reaffirm my view that I strongly disagree with this idea.

It is often argued that [media channels should publish more inspiring stories and positive news]. In my opinion, I agree with this statement only to some extent. While [broadcasting good news motivates citizens to do good deeds], I also believe that [reporting negative incidents is equally vital to warn the public against danger].
column3: The media should include more good stories that report good news. To what extent do you agree and disagree?

column1: On the one hand, I agree that [increasing positive stories in the media is extremely beneficial]. The main reason is that [uplifting news spreads kindness, praises good actions, and creates wonderful role models for young generations]. As a result, [these good examples motivate youngsters to learn valuable ethics and perform acts of kindness in their own communities]. For example, [stories about brave firefighters risking their lives in burning buildings inspire teenagers to show bravery and compassion towards others]. Therefore, this shows that [positive news spreads moral values and contributes greatly to a better society].

On the other hand, I disagree with the idea that [the media should focus mostly on positive stories and overlook bad events]. This is because [reporting negative situations helps citizens stay alert, condemn illegal activities, and protect themselves]. For instance, [news reports about online scammers and cybercrime explain criminal tactics clearly so that Internet users know how to spot fraudulent traps]. Consequently, [readers and viewers learn practical methods to defend their personal safety and avoid substantial financial losses]. Therefore, [reporting social issues and crimes plays an indispensable role condemning criminals and protecting public safety].

In conclusion, [while sharing positive stories spreads good deeds and inspires younger generations], it is not entirely true that [new agencies should only report good stories because exposing negative events protects the public from crime]. Therefore, I hold the view that this statement should only be accepted to a certain extent.

It is often argued that [spending huge financial budgets on space exploration technology is unjustified because this capital could be used for other vital purposes]. In my opinion, I completely agree with this statement. This is because [space missions consume astronomical amounts of national funds with high risks] and [governments should prioritize pressing public needs such as infrastructure, healthcare, and education].
column3: Some people think investing money in developing technology for space exploration is not justifiable. They believe there are other ways to spend money. To what extent do you agree and disagree?

column1: First of all, the main reason for my view is that [space research demands enormous capital and specialized labor that most countries cannot afford].This means that, [building rockets, satellites, and high-tech launch stations requires billions of dollars without guaranteeing immediate practical returns].As a result, [poor and developing nations find it impossible to keep up with these expensive programs, while their public debts continue to grow]. For example, [a single space mission often costs more than the total annual healthcare budget of a small developing country].Therefore, this shows that [pouring immense public money into space exploration creates unnecessary financial burdens for taxpayers].

Furthermore, another important point to consider is that [governments must solve domestic social issues before exploring other planets]. In other words, [national authorities need to allocate public funds into upgrading transport networks, constructing modern hospitals, and improving rural schools]. This leads to, [immediate improvements in the living standards of citizens and fosters long-term economic development]. For instance, [developing nations that invest in clean water systems, public roads, and healthcare facilities can quickly reduce poverty and disease]. Consequently, [using public budgets to address essential human needs on Earth is far more justified than funding space adventures].

In conclusion, [funding space exploration] brings significant negative impacts. The primary reasons are that [outer space projects are prohibitively expensive] and [national funds are urgently needed to upgrade public infrastructure and welfare]. Therefore, I reaffirm my view that I strongly agree with this idea.

It is often argued that providing better public education is a more effective solution to crime than putting people in prison.  In my opinion, I agree with this statement only to some extent. While a good education system helps reduce crime rates in the long term, I also believe that prison is an essential tool to punish dangerous criminals immediately.
column3: Prison is the common way most countries try to solve the problem of crime. However, a more effective solution is to provide the public with a better education. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

column1: On the one hand, I agree that improving public education is very useful in tackling crime. The main reason is that education helps citizens understand the law and distinguish between right and wrong actions. This means that educated people have better moral values and can make wise decisions in difficult situations. For example, when educated individuals face financial problems, they choose to work hard to earn money instead of stealing from others. Therefore, this shows that promoting good education can reduce the crime rate and make society safer.

On the other hand, I disagree with the idea that education is always more effective than imprisonment. This is because severe crimes like riots, violent attacks, and property destruction need immediate physical punishment to deter offenders. Consequently, simply educating criminals without strict punishment cannot protect public order during dangerous incidents. For instance, when football riots break out and aggressive cross loot luxury stores or destroy street facilities, police must put these individuals into prison immediately. Therefore, prison remains an indispensable measure to deter dangerous behaviors and ensure community safety.

In conclusion, while a good education system is a great way to prevent crime from an early age, it is not entirely true that it can replace prisons because severe offenses require strict containment. Therefore, I hold the view that this statement should only be accepted to a certain extent.

It is often argued that [constructing tall apartment blocks is the best method to provide enough home in big cities]. In my opinion, I completely agree with this statement. This is because [urban land resources are extremely limited] and [high-rise buildings make much easier for authorities to manage urban planning].
column3: The best way to provide enough homes in large cities is to build tall apartment blocks. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?

column1: First of all, the main reason for the view is that [the land area in metropolitan cities is strictly limited]. This means that [urban populations are becoming increasingly crowded, while available residential land cannot expand]. As a result, [constructing tall apartment blocks allows cities to house thousands of families on a relatively small piece of land]. For instance, [megacities like Tokyo and Hong Kong rely heavily on high-rise residential towers to solve their severe housing shortages]. Therefore, this shows that [high-rise construction is the most practical solution to accommodate rapid population growth].

Furthermore, another important point to consider is that [apartment complexes help local governments manage populations and develop public amenities efficiently]. In other words, [when residents live close together in vertical buildings, city planners can easily design transport links, water supplies, and electricity grids]. This leads to [well-planned communities where local authorities can build schools, supermarkets and clinics right near residential areas]. For example, [modern apartment projects often integrate green parks, bus stops, and private security systems in one single compound]. Consequently, [building high-rise towers is a vital strategy for efficient city management and sustainable development].

In conclusion, [constructing tall apartment blocks] brings significant impacts. The primary reasons are that [it optimizes limited land resources] and [helps governments develop public infrastructure smoothly]. Therefore, I reaffirm my view that I strongly agree with this idea.

It is often argued that [the growing use of computers and mobile phones for communication harms the reading and writing skills of young people]. In my opinion, I agree with this statement only to some extent. While [digital devices encourage informal writing and short reading habits], I also believe that [they provide helpful tools and daily opportunities to practice language skills].
column3: Some people think that the increasing use of computers and mobile phones for communication has a negative effect on young people’s reading and writing skills. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

column1: On the one hand, I agree that [relying heavily on digital communication negatively impacts young people’s literacy skills]. The main reason is that [teenagers often use text abbreviations, slang words, and emojis instead of proper grammar and full sentences when chatting online]. As a result, [many students forget correct spelling rules and struggle to write formal essays in school exams]. For example, [young users frequently write short forms like “u” or “thx” in text messages, and they accidentally bring these habits into academic assignments]. Therefore, this shows that [casual online chatting reduces young people’s ability to write formally and read long texts patiently].

On the other hand, I disagree with the idea that [computers and smartphones are completely harmful to reading and writing]. This is because [young people actually read and write much more frequently every day through social media posts, emails, and online articles]. Consequently, [regular exposure to digital texts helps youngsters expand their vocabulary and learn how to express opinions quickly]. For instance, [modern smartphones also include built-in spell checkers and grammar dictionaries that immediately help students notice and fix their writing mistakes]. Therefore, [digital devices offer practical learning environments that support young people’s  daily communication skills].

In conclusion, while [frequent digital chatting can encourage bad spelling habits and reduce deep reading], it is not entirely true because [these devices also increase daily reading practice and offer useful language tools]. Therefore, I hold the view that this idea should only be accepted to a certain extent.

It is often argued that [the proliferation of computers and smartphones for communication adversely affects adolescents’ literacy skills]. In my opinion, I agree with this statement only to some extent. While [digital communication undoubtedly fosters casual writing habits and shorter attention spans], I also believe that [technological devices provide unprecedented access to reading materials and automated language-learning aids].

On the one hand, I agree that [excessive reliance on electronic communication deteriorates the formal reading and writing abilities of youngsters]. The main reason is that [instant messaging platforms prioritize speed over grammatical accuracy, encouraging teenagers to adopt internet slang, acronyms, and fragmented sentences]. As a result, [young learners gradually lose proficiency in academic composition and struggle to comprehend complex, long-form literature]. For example, [high school students accustomed to skimming brief social media captions often find it exhausting to analyze dense academic textbooks or write coherent essays]. Therefore, this shows that [informal digital habits can erode traditional literacy standards it left unchecked].

On the other hand, I disagree with the idea that [modern devices exert a purely detrimental impact on young people’s linguistic development]. This is because [contemporary youth engage with written content far more frequently than previous generations through digital news outlets, online forums, and interactive blogs]. Consequently, [continuous engagement with diverse digital texts broadens their vocabulary and enhances their ability to articulate ideas across global platforms]. For instance, [integrated software features such as real-time spell checkers, predictive text, and digital thesauruses enable students to identify syntactic errors and refine their writing style autonomously]. Therefore, [digital technology serves as a powerful catalyst for daily literacy practice when utilized responsibly].

In conclusion, while [digital communication platforms can undermine formal grammatical precision and deep reading endurance], it is not entirely true because [they simultaneously stimulate frequent text engagement and offer intelligent editing tools]. Therefore, I hold the view that this idea should only be accepted to a certain extent.

There is an ongoing debate surrounding whether [zoos are cruel places that should be shut down permanently], or if they should [play an important role in saving wild animals]. While I acknowledge that [keeping animals in small cages can harm their natural instincts], I firmly believe that [modern zoos are essential for protecting endangered species and educating the public].
column3: Some people think that zoos are all cruel and should be closed down. Others however believe that zoos can be useful in protecting wild animals. Discuss both opinions and give your own opinion.

column1: On the one hand, there are several convincing reasons why [some people believe zoos are cruel and should be closed]. The primary reason is that [wild animals are kept in small artificial cages instead of living freely in their natural habitats]. For instance, [large predators like lions and bears often suffer from severe stress and depression because they lack open space to hunt and run]. In addition, [some poorly managed zoos prioritize making money from visitors rather than providing proper medical care and nutritious food for their animals]. Consequently, [keeping creatures locked up for human entertainment violates animal rights and damages their physical health].

On the other hand, I am equally in favor of the opinion that [zoos serve a vital purpose in wildlife conservation]. Firstly, [zoos protect endangered animals from illegal poachers and habitat destruction by providing safe shelters and professional veterinary care]. For example, [successful breeding programs inside zoos have saved rare species like the giant panda from complete extinction]. Secondly, [visiting zoos allows children and adults to learn directly about biodiversity and understand the importance of protecting nature]. Therefore, [well-managed zoos are indispensable institutions for preserving rare wildlife and raising public awareness].

In conclusion, it is undeniable that [keeping animals in poor, cramped cages causes physical and mental suffering]. However, [modern zoos] are equally indispensable for [their breeding programs and educational value in protecting endangered creatures]. Therefore, I hold the belief that instead of closing all zoos down, governments should strictly regulate them to ensure high standards of animal welfare.

There is ongoing debate surrounding whether [zoological parks are inhumane institutions that ought to be permanently abolished], or if they [serve a crucial function in wildlife preservation]. While I acknowledge that [confining creatures in artificial enclosures can compromise their psychological well-being], I firmly believe that [zoos are indispensable for safeguarding endangered species and fostering environment education].

On the one hand, there are several convincing reasons why [opponents contend that zoos are inherently cruel and warrant closure]. The primary reason is that [captivity deprives wild creatures of their natural freedom and forces them into cramped, unnatural environments]. For instance, [wide-ranging mammals such as tigers and elephants frequently exhibit repetitive, stress-induced behaviors when restricted to limited spaces that prevent instinctive hunting or migration]. In addition, [profit-driven facilities often neglect animal welfare by prioritizing commercial ticket sales over adequate veterinary nutrition and habitat enrichment]. Consequently, [confining sentient being purely for public amusement constitutes ethical exploitation and deteriorates their physical vitality].

On the other hand, I am equally in favour of the opinion that [modern zoological facilities play a pivotal role in biodiversity conservation]. Firstly, [accredited zoos act as vital sanctuaries that shield vulnerable species from rampant poaching, deforestation, and climate threats through specialized medical care]. For example, [controlled captive-breeding initiatives have successfully revitalized populations of critically endangered species, such as the Arabian oryx and the giant panda, before reintroducing them into the wild]. Secondly, [zoos offer immersive educational experiences that inspire visitors to appreciate wildlife and support ecological protection policies]. Therefore, [responsible zoos represent essential refuges for preventing mass extinction and cultivating conservation awareness].

In conclusion, it is undeniable that [substandard zoos inflict unnecessary distress by depriving animals of their natural habitats]. However, [well-regulated zoological institutions are equally indispensable for executing life-saving breeding programs and educating society about environmental stewardship]. Therefore, I hold the belief that rather than shutting zoos down entirely, authorities should enforce strict welfare regulations to transform them into true conservation centers.

It is often argued that the [extinction of animal species is a completely natural process like what happened to dinosaurs, so humans should not try to stop it]. In my opinion, I completely disagree with this statement. This is because [modern extinction is mainly caused by destructive human activities] and [saving wildlife is essential to protect the ecosystem and human survival].
column3: It is natural for animal species, including dinosaurs, to go extinct, and people should not attempt to prevent it. Do you support or oppose this idea? Explain your viewpoint with reasons and include appropriate examples based on your knowledge or experiences. (Agree or disagree)

column1: First of all, the main reason for my view is that [unlike dinosaurs that died out from disasters, most animals today disappear because of human actions]. This means that [illegal hunting, forest destruction, and industrial pollution and destroying wild habitats much faster than nature can recover]. As a result, [thousands of rare species are dying out unnaturally before they can adapt to the changing environment]. For example, [rhinos and elephants are critically endangered primarily because poachers kill them for ivory and horns rather than due to natural evolution]. Therefore, [humans have a moral responsibility to fix the ecological damage they have directly caused].

Furthermore, another important point to consider is that [every species plays a vital role in keeping the natural ecosystem balanced]. In other words, [if one animal species becomes extinct, it will disrupt the food chain and negatively affect many other plants, animals, and humans]. This leads to [severe environmental problems such as crop failures, pest outbreaks, and the loss of clean natural resources]. For instance, [if honeybees disappear completely, global agriculture will collapse because crops cannot be pollinated effectively]. Consequently, [preventing animal extinction is crucial for protecting biodiversity and ensuring a safe future for humanity].

In conclusion, [letting animal species go extinct without taking action brings devastating consequences to our planet]. The primary reasons are that [current extinction rates are driven by human destruction and losing wildlife threatens the natural balance that humans depend on]. Therefore, I reaffirm my view that I strongly oppose the idea of ignoring animal extinction.

It is often argued that [the extinction of animal species is an inevitable natural phenomenon comparable to the disappearance of dinosaurs, and humanity should therefore refrain from intervening]. In my opinion, I completely disagree with this statement. This is because [contemporary mass extinction is predominantly triggered by anthropogenic destruction] and [preserving biodiversity is vital for maintaining ecological stability and human survival].

First of all, the main reason for my view is that [unlike prehistoric species that vanished due to natural cataclysms, modern wildlife is disappearing rapidly because of human exploitation]. This means that [rampant deforestation, industrial pollution, and climate change are obliterating natural habitats at an unprecedented pace]. As a result, [vulnerable creatures are pushed toward species such as Sumatran tigers and Javan rhinos face imminent annihilation primarily due to illegal poaching and agricultural expansion rather than natural selection]. Therefore, [humans bear an ethical obligation to halt this accelerated loss of wildlife that they have directly instigated].

Furthermore, another important point to consider is that [every organism performs an irreplaceable ecological function within the global food web]. In other words, [the eradication of a single keystone species can trigger a domino effect that destabilizes entire ecosystems and diminishes vital natural resources]. This leads to [severe agricultural and medical crises that directly endanger human welfare]. For instance, [the rapid decline of pollinating insects like honeybees threatens global food security, while losing rare rainforest fauna deprives scientists of potential breakthroughs in pharmaceutical medicine]. Consequently, [active wildlife conservation is indispensable not merely for saving animals, but for safeguarding the biosphere that sustains human civilization].

In conclusion, [allowing animal species to perish without conservation efforts yields catastrophic repercussions for the natural world]. The primary reasons are that [current extinction crises stem largely from human interference] and [preserving ecological diversity is essential].

In recent years, there has been a noticeable shift towards [replacing traditional fossil fuels with renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power]. Although I understand why some people view this as a negative development, I still consider it to be a largely positive trend.
column3: Fossil fuels, such as coal, oil and natural gas, are the main source for many countries. However, some nations are using alternative energy such as solar power and wind power. Do you think this is a positive or negative development?

column1: There are several reasons why this trend can be seen as a negative development. The primary concern is that [building renewable energy infrastructure requires huge initial financial investments]. For instance, [developing countries often struggle to pay for expensive solar panels, giant wind turbines, and modern power grids]. In addition, [clean energy sources depend heavily on unstable weather conditions]. This means that [solar panels cannot produce electricity at night, and wind turbines stop working when there is no wind]. As a result, [governments may face sudden power shortages if they stop using coal and natural gas too quickly].

Nevertheless, I am in favor of the opinion that this is a positive development for several reasons. Firstly, [alternative energy helps reduce air pollution and slow down global warming]. For example, [unlike coal power plants, solar and wind farms do not release harmful greenhouse gases into the atmosphere]. Secondly, [natural resources like sunlight and wind are unlimited and will never run out]. Consequently, [countries can achieve long-term energy independence instead of importing expensive foreign oil]. Therefore, [switching to green energy creates a cleaner environment and sustainable future for everyone].

In conclusion, despite understanding why some critics view [then transition to alternative energy] as a negative trend due to [high setup costs and weather dependency]. I still believe that its positive contributions to [environmental protection and sustainable power supply] are far more profound. Therefore, I hold the belief that this is ultimately a positive development.

In recent years, there has been a noticeable shift towards [utilizing renewable energy alternatives, such as solar and wind power, instead of relying solely on conventional fossil fuels]. Although I understand why some people view this as a negative development, I still consider it to be a largely positive trend.

There are several reasons why this trend can be seen as a negative development. The primary concern is that [transitioning to green power systems demands substantial upfront capital and advanced grid infrastructure]. For instance, [emerging economies frequently encounter severe budgetary constraints when installing large-scale offshore wind farms and high-capacity battery storage facilities]. In addition, [renewable power generation is inherently intermittent because it fluctuates according to climatic patterns]. This means that [electricity output drops significantly during prolonged cloudy periods or calm weather without sufficient wind velocity]. As a result, [national power grids risk experiencing instability and blackouts unless expensive backup systems are maintained].
